title: Two divergent CSV parsers: job host import silently corrupts CSVs the app itself wrote
existing_state: CsvManager contains two independent CSV parsers. The grid load path uses ReadCsvRecord (CsvManager.cs:118-189), a full record reader that supports quoted fields with embedded newlines — and the app's own save path deliberately produces such fields: EscapeCsvValue quotes any value containing \n or \r (CsvManager.cs:254-256). The second parser, public static ParseCsvLine (CsvManager.cs:194-243), is line-based and cannot handle embedded newlines. JobStorageService.ImportHostsFromCsv uses the second one: it does File.ReadAllLines and parses each physical line independently (JobStorageService.cs:263-285, delegating at 311-312). Result: a hosts CSV exported by the app's own Save (or any RFC-compliant CSV) containing a multi-line cell loads perfectly into the main grid but, when imported into a scheduled job, splits the quoted record across lines — the first fragment becomes a short row and the continuation line becomes a bogus extra 'host' — with no error. The job then targets a corrupted host list.
recommendation: Delete the duplication: expose the record-based reader (ReadCsvRecord, or a LoadFromFile overload returning rows) as the single parsing entry point and rewrite JobStorageService.ImportHostsFromCsv to stream records through it instead of File.ReadAllLines + ParseCsvLine. Keep ParseCsvLine only if a genuinely single-line use case remains, and document it as such.
user_benefit: Job host imports stop silently diverging from grid imports for the same file — no phantom hosts or truncated rows in scheduled jobs, and one parser to fix when the next CSV edge case shows up.

evidence.note: Record reader handles embedded newlines; ParseCsvLine does not; EscapeCsvValue emits quoted newlines on save
ImportHostsFromCsv: File.ReadAllLines + per-line ParseCsvLine — breaks on quoted multi-line fields
